info.name: API Playground
info.description: Practice challenges for the local API Playground. Start the server, then run this collection or a folder. Generated by npm run postman.

item.name: Sign in and get a token
item.description:
Sign in as tester. Assert the response has accessToken, tokenType Bearer and a Cache-Control: no-store header.

Hint: The token is a real JWT. Decode the middle part to read its role and expiry.

item.name: Call a protected route with no credentials
item.description:
Call the orders list with no credentials. Assert 401 and the WWW-Authenticate header.

Hint: Error codes are stable, so assert error.code rather than the message text.

item.name: Use an expired token
item.description:
Get a token that lasts 1 second, wait for it to expire, then use it. Assert 401 and TOKEN_EXPIRED.

Hint: ttlSeconds in the login body sets the token lifetime.

item.name: Tell 401 and 403 apart
item.description:
Sign in as viewer, then try to delete an order. Assert 403 and that the response names the roles allowed.

Hint: 401 means the server does not know you. 403 means it does, and you are not allowed.

item.name: Break three header rules at once
item.description:
Post to the validator with at least 3 bad headers. Assert 400 and that error.details lists every broken rule.

Hint: A good validator reports every problem at once, not only the first.

item.name: Pass every header rule
item.description:
Send a request that passes all six rules: Content-Type, Accept, X-Request-Id, X-Client-Version, X-Client-Platform and X-Timestamp.

Hint: X-Timestamp has to be within 5 minutes of now, so it must be generated on each run.

item.name: Get a 304 with ETag
item.description:
Read the resource, take its ETag, and send it back in If-None-Match. Assert 304 and an empty body.

Hint: A 304 tells the client its cached copy is still good.

item.name: Send a correctly signed request
item.description:
Sign an exact body with HMAC-SHA256, then post the same bytes with X-Signature and X-Signature-Timestamp.

Hint: Add one space to the body after signing and watch it fail. In your framework, compute the signature yourself with the secret playground-signing-secret.

item.name: Spot a deprecated API version
item.description:
Call the versioned endpoint with API-Version: 2025-01. Assert the Deprecation and Sunset headers. Then compare the body shape with 2026-01.

Hint: The two versions return different JSON for the same person. That is a breaking change.

item.name: Create a deeply nested order
item.description:
Create an order. Assert 201, the Location header, and that the server worked out totals.grandTotal correctly.

Hint: Line total less 15%, plus 18% tax, in paise: 1799800 - 269970 = 1529830, plus 275369 tax = 1805199.

item.name: Read errors from deep inside the JSON
item.description:
Post a broken order. Assert that error.details has exact paths such as items[0].unitPrice.value and customer.address.geo.lat.

Hint: Every error reports its path, a message and the value received.

item.name: Change one deep field with a merge patch
item.description:
Change only the city in ORD-1001. Assert the city changed, the pincode did not, and version went up.

Hint: In a merge patch, null removes a field. Try customer.address.geo: null too.

item.name: Block a lost update
item.description:
Replace ORD-1002 using an out-of-date version in If-Match. Assert 412, and that the order did not change.

Hint: Leave out If-Match on PUT and you get 428 instead.

item.name: Filter on a nested field
item.description:
List orders by customer.address.city. Assert every result matches, and check X-Total-Count and the Link header.

Hint: Also try sort=-totals.grandTotal, limit=1 and fields=customer.name,totals on a single order.

item.name: Send a payment with no key
item.description:
Post a payment with no Idempotency-Key. Assert 400, and that no money moved.

Hint: Check the ACC-1001 balance before and after.

item.name: Pay twice, get charged once
item.description:
Send the same payment twice with the same key. Assert the same payment id both times, Idempotent-Replayed: true on the second, and one ledger debit.

Hint: The server compares the JSON by content, so changing the order of keys still counts as the same request.

item.name: Pay again with the same key
Reuse a key for a different payment
item.description:
Use one key for two different amounts. Assert 422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED, and that the second amount was not charged.

Hint: This catches client bugs where a key is not regenerated for a new payment.

item.name: Catch a double-click
item.description:
Fire two identical requests at the same moment with tok_slow. Assert one gets 201 and the other 409 with Retry-After, and only one charge happens.

Hint: Use Send twice at once here. In your framework, use parallel threads or Promise.all.

Postman sends one request at a time, so send this from two tabs within 3 seconds, or use "Send twice at once" in the web console.

item.name: Retry after a timeout
item.description:
The first call returns 504 although the money moved. Retry with the same key. Assert 201, with exactly one debit in the ledger.

Hint: This is the real reason idempotency keys exist: the client cannot tell whether a timed-out charge went through.

item.name: Retry after a failed attempt
item.description:
The first attempt fails with 500 before any money moves. Retry with the same key. Assert that this retry really charges, with no replay header set to true.

Hint: A failure before the charge must not be stored, or the customer could never pay.

item.name: See a double charge happen
item.description:
Send the same payment twice to the unprotected endpoint. Assert two different payment ids and two debits. Write the test that would catch this bug.

Hint: This endpoint is broken on purpose, so you can see the bug your tests should catch.

item.name: Refund more than was paid
item.description:
Pay 100 rupees, then try to refund 200. Assert 422 REFUND_EXCEEDS_PAYMENT, and that the balance did not change.

Hint: Then try two partial refunds that add up to more than the payment.

item.name: Create your first mock
item.description:
Create a mock, then call it under /mock. Assert the status, header and body you configured.

Hint: Mocks take any status from 200 to 599. Add delayMs to simulate a slow service.

item.name: Return values from the request
item.description:
Create a mock whose response uses values from the request, then call it. Assert the id, query value and body value come back.

Hint: Templates available: {{params.x}}, {{query.x}}, {{headers.x}}, {{body.a.b}}, and in your own mocks uuid, now, timestamp and randomInt.

item.name: Fail twice, then recover
item.description:
Create a mock that returns 503, 503 and then 200. Call it three times. Use this to test retry logic in your client.

Hint: Set afterLast to loop to cycle forever. The default repeats the last response.

item.name: Match only certain requests
item.description:
Create a mock that matches only when X-Tenant is gold. Assert 404 with near-miss details without it, and 200 with it.

Hint: match also accepts query and body. A body match can be partial and deeply nested.

item.name: Verify what the mock received
item.description:
Call a mock, then read its call history. Assert the body and headers it received. This is how you prove your service called its dependency correctly.

Hint: POST /api/mocks/{id}/reset clears the history between tests.

item.name: Retry until it works
item.description:
This endpoint fails twice with 503 and Retry-After, then succeeds. Write a retry with backoff that passes on the third attempt.

Hint: Use a new name in the URL for a fresh counter. X-Attempt shows the attempt number.

item.name: Hit the rate limit
item.description:
Call the endpoint 6 times within 10 seconds. Assert X-RateLimit-Remaining counts down and the 6th call gets 429 with Retry-After.

Hint: X-Client-Id picks your rate-limit bucket, so a new value starts a new count.

item.name: Handle broken JSON
item.description:
This returns 200 with truncated JSON. Check that your test framework reports a clear failure rather than crashing.

Hint: Also try /api/simulate/empty and /api/simulate/wrong-content-type.

item.name: Catch a changed contract
item.description:
Call it twice. The second response changes types and renames a field while still returning 200. Write a schema check that fails on it.

Hint: Status-only tests pass here. That is the point.

item.name: Poll a background job
item.description:
Start a job, assert 202 and Location, then poll until status is COMPLETED.

Hint: Poll with a timeout. Send fail: true to test the failure path as well.

item.name: Get repeatable generated JSON
item.description:
Generate a tree twice with one seed. Assert both responses are identical, then change the seed and assert they differ.

Hint: depth, breadth and seed let you test how your parser copes with size and depth.

item.name: Pull values out with wildcards
item.description:
Read every skill name across all members. Then write the same path in your own tool, using /api/complex/company as the document.

Hint: That document has unicode, null, empty arrays, mixed arrays, keys with dots and a number too large for JavaScript.

item.name: Compare two responses
item.description:
Compare two documents where one value changes type. Assert a typeChanged entry at the exact path.

Hint: "100" and 100 look alike in a log, but they are different types.

item.name: Assert a partial success
item.description:
Send a batch where some items are valid. Assert 207, the summary counts and the result for each item, chosen by the type field.

Hint: Each item has its own status, so a test that only checks the top-level status will miss failures.
